q: Fix this overlay. The BME280 on `i2c1` is never found: `DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_NODELABEL(env_sensor))` won't even build. The board's `.dts` has `&i2c1 { status = "disabled"; ... }`.
options: Add `status = "okay";` to `&i2c1`: a sensor on a disabled bus has no controller device to talk through
explain: The sensor node itself is `okay` (a missing `status` means okay, and `status` isn't inherited from the parent), so the BME280 driver is built for it. But that driver instance needs the `i2c1` controller device, and the board left `i2c1` disabled, so that device was never defined and compiling the BME280 driver fails (`__device_dts_ord_N` undeclared, N being the bus node). Enable the bus. 0x76 is the correct I2C address (the unit address `@76` is hex too). The label `env_sensor:` is what `DT_NODELABEL` uses, and node names can stay as they are. Kconfig symbols go in `.conf` files, never in a devicetree overlay.

q: Which snippet gets the board's LED portably, so it works on any board that defines a `led0` alias, with polarity handled?
options: `static const struct gpio_dt_spec led = GPIO_DT_SPEC_GET(DT_ALIAS(led0), gpios);` then `gpio_pin_set_dt(&led, 1);`
`static const struct gpio_dt_spec led = GPIO_DT_SPEC_GET(DT_NODELABEL(led0), gpios);`
explain: `DT_ALIAS(led0)` follows the board's alias. `GPIO_DT_SPEC_GET` pulls the port, pin *and flags* (such as `GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW`) from the tree, so `gpio_pin_set_dt(&led, 1)` means logical "on" on every board. Hard-coding the pin and polarity defeats the point. `device_get_binding` with a string name is the old runtime lookup. `led0` is an *alias*, not a node label, so `DT_NODELABEL(led0)` only works if a board happens to use that label too.

q: Order these from "hardware described" to "code using it safely".
items: An overlay adds `bme280@76` with `compatible = "bosch,bme280"` under an `okay` `&i2c0`
The binding YAML for `bosch,bme280` validates the node's properties at build time
The generated devicetree header provides macros for the node
`DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_NODELABEL(bme))` resolves to the driver instance at compile/link time
At startup, `device_is_ready(bme)` confirms the driver's init succeeded
explain: The tree describes the hardware. The binding (matched by `compatible`) checks it, and bad or missing properties fail the build. The generator turns it into macros. `DEVICE_DT_GET` turns a node into a `const struct device *` at build time (a missing or disabled node fails the build, not a NULL at runtime). Finally `device_is_ready()` covers what the build can't know: did the sensor actually answer during init?

q: Fix this overlay. The status LED moved from P0.13 to P0.17 on rev B of your PCB. Which change is idiomatic?
options: Edit the board's `.dts` in the Zephyr tree
`#ifdef REV_B` around the pin number in `main.c`
explain: Overlays are merged on top of the board's tree. Referencing the node by its label (`&status_led`) and overriding one property is the whole change, and the C code doesn't change at all. Editing upstream board files breaks with every SDK update. `#ifdef`s put hardware back into code, and there's no such Kconfig symbol, because pins are hardware, so they live in the devicetree.

q: Which statements about devicetree in Zephyr are true?
options: It's compiled into C macros at build time, so there's no runtime parsing
`status = "disabled"` nodes still get a driver instance, they just aren't started
`build/zephyr/zephyr.dts` shows the final merged tree after all overlays
Devicetree replaces Kconfig: you no longer need `CONFIG_` options for drivers
explain: Zephyr resolves the tree at build time into `DT_*` macros. Disabled nodes get **no** instance at all. `chosen` and `aliases` are the indirections that keep code portable, and `zephyr.dts` in the build directory is the merged truth to check when debugging. Devicetree describes *hardware* and Kconfig selects *software*, so you need both (though many driver symbols default to `y` when an enabled node exists).
